measured: the applications the demand scan reads (twin-world demand/applications.json), in its clones (~/.cache/twin-demand) at the commits twin-world's generated/demand.json names, each grepped for Supabase (a host, a client, a variable, a document) and each hit followed to its caller. RH2 (volter-ai/runhuman-2 34fdc93) keeps its authority store in a Supabase project's Postgres and speaks the Postgres wire to it and nothing else: "no PostgREST, no Supabase client library, no anon session" (apps/rh2/docs/OPERATIONS.md:255-258); its release migrates the database over its URL (apps/rh2/scripts/release.sh:45, apps/rh2/src/database/migrate-cli.ts:43-48) and its Worker queries it through Hyperdrive with node-postgres (apps/rh2/src/edge/database.ts:3, :87). As a Volter product it is demand in full. twin-world's apps/cloud installs this package (it hosts the pack; no call). Postiz's pnpm-lock lists @supabase/supabase-js only as an optional peer of a langchain package (pnpm-lock.yaml:3966), which Postiz never imports; Dub, Cal.com, Rallly, Twenty, LibreChat, Volter Editor, Supercode and Browser Substrate name Supabase only in documents, icons or regular expressions. Runhuman 1 is not read (owner: "drop runhuman 1 fro that list", demand/applications.json), so its PostgREST, Storage and Management API calls are no demand. No demanded application calls the Management API, PostgREST, Storage or Auth: the demand is the project's database, which a World serves as its managed Postgres, its URL issued by the credential door (twin-world packages/world-runtime/src/init.ts:843).
